Rego
Expressions are now separated by semicolons (instead of commas). When writing rules, the semicolons are optional.
Rules are no longer written in the form: `head :- body`. Instead they are written as `head { body }`.
Set, array, and object literals now support trailing commas.
To declare a set literal with one element, you must include a trailing comma, e.g., `{ foo, }`.
Arithmetic and set operations can now be performed with infix notation, e.g., `x = 2 + 1`.
Sets can be referred to like objects and arrays now. E.g., `p[_].foo = 1 # check if element in has attr foo equal to 1`.

`startswith`, `endswith`, `strings.any_prefix_match` and `strings.any_suffix_match` are indexed when the base strings are known at compile time.

References rooted at a local variable (`x := input; x.foo == "a"`) are indexed the same as `input.foo == "a"`, and a chain of assignments no longer drops the constraint at the end of it.
A rule's path through the trie stops at the last level it constrains, and a reference reached by several values no longer leaves the rest of the rule unindexed.
